sentences.text:
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice C.V.Bhaskar Reddy
 Writ Petition No.19974 of 2024
Order:

This writ petition has been filed seeking to declare the action of respondent Nos.2 to 4 in not depositing the compensation amount of Rs.9,27,826/- in respect of acquired land, admeasuring 100 square yards in Survey No.606 situated at Boyapalli Village, Tandur Mandal, Mancherial Dsitrict, in the account of Hanuman Temple, vide its Account No.79075076715 of Telangana Grameena Bank,
Tandur Branch, Mancherial District, vide IFSC Code No.SBIN0RRDCGB which is acquired by the respondents under National Highways Act for laning of NH 363 from Mancherial to Chandrapur as illegal, arbitrary and violative of principles of natural justice and for other appropriate reliefs.
The petitioner claims to be the Chairman of Hanuman Temple situated at Boyapalli Village, Tandur Mandal, Mancherial District.

The case of the petitioner is that a committee has been constituted for the development of the subject temple, which in turn opened a bank account in the name of the temple in the Telangana Grameena Bank, Tandur Branch, Mancherial District, vide Account No.79075076715.

It is the further case of the petitioner that respondent No.2 acquired an extent of 100 square yards of the temple land forming part of Survey No.606 for the purpose of widening/four- laning of National Highway 363 (Mancherial to Chandrapur Section) and compensation has also been determined for the acquired land under the provisions of the National Highway Act, 1956 to the tune of Rs.9,27,826/-.

The grievance of the petitioner is that even after determination of the compensation payable for the said acquired land of the Temple, despite several representations, the respondents are not depositing the compensation amount into the bank account being maintained in the name of the Temple, vide Account No.79075076715.

Both learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondent Nos.1, 3 and 4 and Mr. Ramu, learned Standing Counsel for National Highways Authority India (NHAI)
appearing for respondent No.2, on instructions, submit that there are multiple claims over the subject land of the temple; and while the petitioner, claiming as Chairman of the Temple, has made a claim for deposit of the compensation amount into the account being maintained in the name of the Temple vide Account No.79075076715, representatives of some of the villagers objected for depositing the compensation amount into the said account of the temple.
Since it appears that there are rival claims over the compensation amount determined in respect of the acquired land of the subject temple, this Court is of the opinion that ends of justice would be met if the respondents are directed to deposit the said compensation amount before the Assistant Commissioner of Endowments, Adilabad, within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order, who in turn shall utilise the same only for the purpose of development of the subject temple, after obtaining approval of the Commissioner of Endowments, and shall submit the Bhima Rajkumar vs The State Of Telangana on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50259138/
